verdict.rationale: Weave's own docs say coding agents can connect through W&B Skills and the MCP server to run evaluations, and that the MCP server lets agents answer questions about evaluations, which covers triggering a run and reading back results. Evaluations are defined programmatically over a Dataset object, and a REST Service API exists. However, there is no explicit evidence of an agent creating and publishing a dataset, and no hands-on corroboration of the end-to-end loop. missing for 10: explicit documentation of agent- or API-driven dataset creation, documented MCP or REST endpoints for programmatically triggering an evaluation and retrieving its scores, independent or hands-on corroboration of the end-to-end agent workflow

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can have an agent create a dataset, trigger an eval run programmatically, and read back the results

citations.quote: Using W&B skills and the MCP server, coding agents like Claude Code connect to Weave. They can read live production data, run evaluations, and execute automatic iteration loops on their own
your agent can answer questions about your runs, traces, evaluations, and artifacts without copy-paste.
Skills covers both the [W\&B Models SDK] ... and the [Weave SDK] (traces, evaluations, scorers).
the core of the workflow is the _`Evaluation` object_, which defines: A `Dataset` or list of dictionaries for test examples. One or more scoring functions.
Use the Weave Service API, which provides REST endpoints for programmatic access to Weave functionality.
